competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency names fractions 'equal to one and greater than one,' yet the target fraction in every sample — 1/6, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 — is a proper fraction strictly less than one, so the exact quantity the competency asks students to represent never appears as a correct answer.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Of the two named sub-cases, none of the eight samples asks a student to model a fraction equal to one (like 6/6) or greater than one (like 3/2); the closest any correct_answer gets to one is seed43's '1/2'.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The repeated template 'A shape is divided into N equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?' with small denominators (2, 4, 6, 8) is short, concrete and well within grade-3 reading and reasoning demand, independent of the scope problem flagged elsewhere.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four formatters appear (mcq, read_mcq, set_click, cloze) but the underlying model shown never changes shape — every sample is exactly one part shaded out of N — so no variant ever shows a fully-shaded whole (N/N) or a model spanning more than one whole.

competency_alignment.rationale: Values at or above one surface only as rejected distractors, e.g. seed42's own option list offers '6/1' as wrong and seed43 offers '2/1' and '3/2' as wrong, meaning the variation actually trained is 'pick the proper fraction,' the opposite of what 'represent ... equal to one and greater than one' asks for.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Across all eight rendered samples the largest correct_answer value is 1/2 (seed43, seed46, seed55, seed72) — the observed range never touches the competency's own floor of one, let alone extends above it.
